correctness.rationale: Haar Weyl integration and Peter–Weyl characters give exact K_L sin² theta=−m cos(2m theta)+(1/2)cot(theta)sin(2m theta). The convolution endpoint norm equals its Haar L1 mass. b_m decreasing, bounded 1/u; mean-zero signed oscillations and O(1/R) sign-switch errors allow limiting subtraction and the exact improper integral. Each period contribution is negative: J0=Si(pi)−2<0, and for k≥1 T_a≥(pi−2)/B²>E_a using the bound (1−8/(15pi²))^-2<pi−2. The resulting period series has O(k^-2) tail and is strictly negative. Numerical script checks finite-band identities and root series; these are not treated as proofs.

value.rationale: Sharp additive amplification error for the natural unsmoothed integer-spin SO(3) Peter–Weyl cutoff is a motivated quantitative refinement of leading growth. It identifies a strictly negative universal boundary-layer effect and a convergent root-series evaluable independently. This cannot be read off from the leading SU(2) full-spectrum law because the frequency mask and absolute values differ. Distinguishes actual finite-band overshoot/deficit in rotation-group harmonic reconstruction.
